name: CA-15
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Mullin has raised roughly $980,000 while the challenger shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
No public polling; outlook rests on district fundamentals
model.rationale: A D+26 district, an incumbent who has vastly out-raised an essentially unfunded challenger, and market pricing near 96% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold. With no polling available, the margin estimate rests on district fundamentals, which leave little room for an upset.
model.watch: Only an unexpected scandal or external event affecting Mullin would put this seat in play; no polling or spending signal currently suggests competitive activity.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 15th District leans Democratic by 26 points, and incumbent Kevin Mullin is seeking another term after advancing to the general election. He has raised roughly $980,000 for the race, while Republican Charles Hoelter shows no reported fundraising, cash on hand, or outside support in the available data. No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, but prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96 percent.

The combination of a heavily Democratic electorate, an established incumbent, and a large financial asymmetry makes an upset unlikely. Districts this partisan typically produce margins well above twenty points even against funded challengers, and Hoelter's campaign appears minimally resourced. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of direct polling rather than any sign of competitive activity on the ground.
